items.title: Carl Allen interviewed by Monk Rowe, Atlanta, Georgia, January 4, 2013
items.q: I mean we don’t say uh, Wagner again? Chopin again?

ctx.x: And so I’m wondering well, is that true and what should they be playing instead?

Well I guess you have to know your audience. I think that’s a big part of it. But I disagree with the principle that the American songbook is killing jazz. Why? How could it be doing that? I don’t get that. You know the thing that’s always amazed me is this attempt to always want to recreate what jazz is. We don’t do that with classical music. I mean we don’t say uh, Wagner again? Chopin again? We don’t do that. It’s like it’s great music why not appreciate it for what it is? I have personal theories about why I…

And I just want to, as an aside, you use the word triplet with your students to define the swinging eighth note — the first two notes tied together. Do you verbalize that to them? How would you verbalize that to them?
